name: Air cooling (CRAH/CRAC, hot/cold aisle containment)
applications: Cooling racks up to roughly 20 kW
Retrofit cooling where liquid cooling is not warranted
principle: Air cooling moves heat from the rack to a room coil and then to outdoor air or a chilled-water loop. Containment separates the cold supply from the hot return so the coil sees the rack outlet temperature instead of a mixed room average. The architecture stops being practical somewhere around 20 kW per rack, which is where liquid cooling enters.

process_steps.name: Cooled air is supplied into the cold aisle
Server fans draw air through IT equipment
Containment carries hot return air back to the coil
Coil transfers heat to chilled water or refrigerant

performance.basis: Vertiv article on rear-door heat exchangers: the practical limit for air cooling is around 20 kW per rack, which is where rear-door and other liquid approaches start.

source.note: Vertiv, How rear door heat exchangers (RDHx) support high-density rack cooling, read 2026-11-14

performance.metric: installed share of racks below 10 kW, 2024 to 2025
performance.basis: Vertiv figure on installed racks: racks below 10 kW fell from 47 percent in 2024 to 38 percent in 2025; 10-20 kW rose from 27 to 30 percent and 20-30 kW from 24 to 28 percent, so air-cooled densities are shrinking as a share.

source.note: Vertiv, How rear door heat exchangers (RDHx) support high-density rack cooling, read 2026-11-14

performance.metric: unit cooling capacity, Vertiv Liebert DSE free-cooling system
performance.basis: Liebert DSE product page: 50-165 kW standard range, with packaged units around 250-400 kW; water-free operation.

source.note: Vertiv Liebert DSE free-cooling system 50-165 kW product page, read 2026-11-12

advantages: Lowest cost per kW of cooling at low density
Simple to maintain and well understood by operators
No facility water and no liquid in the white space
limitations: Practical limit around 20 kW per rack
Cooling is 7-30 percent of data centre electricity, the largest parasitic load
Containment discipline decays without operational enforcement
